Survivors of the 29 mutants: two. Both are equivalent, so each gets a one-line note and needs no test.
* **K-S3half** drops the module-side `realpathSync` in `isMain`. Under Node's default resolution, `import.meta.url` is
  already the real path. Under `--preserve-symlinks-main`, or with `--preserve-symlinks` through a linked folder, the
  linked script cannot load at all: probed in the mirror, `node --preserve-symlinks-main <link>/paths.mjs` exits 1 with
  an uncaught module error, with and without the mutant. So no run of the script separates the two forms. CONFIRMED.
* **K-S3guard** drops `if (!process.argv[1]) return false`. `realpathSync(undefined)` then throws inside the `try`, and
  the `catch` returns false, which is the same result.

## (2) The refusal census (J264, N-58)

The lint registers no B-FUZZ family, register or seed sweep, so its census is the refusal of lawful input over the
tree. To get the before state, this checker put back the round's two behaviour changes in the mirror (`BENCH_CODE` with
the before regex; `isMain` in the bare-equality form). `node scripts/lint.mjs` then exits 0. With the round's code it
also exits 0. The two outputs are identical line for line (both `eslint 1156 files, 0 errors`, probe-red 10/10, 9 checks
ok). Lawful-input refusals: **0 → 0**, so the count did not rise. CONFIRMED.

The one new refusal class is a `.jsx` file in a KERNEL bench folder that reaches a town package. That input is
UNLAWFUL by C-0259 (4)'s bench boundary. Its verdict is REFUSE, typed and visible as `bench/<folder>/<file>.jsx:<line>:
a KERNEL bench (bench/<folder>) reaches @plat/<pkg>` (CONFIRMED by the test above). The alternative is
`bench/manifest.json`'s TOWN and INFRA folders, which may import a town package. This checker saw no lawful-input
refusal.
